occurrenceRemarks: Our group took a whale shark tour, traveling from the port at 0800 around 1 hour to Parque Nacional Isla Contoy ($10 fee to enter). We drove around for about 45 minutes before the guide said this individual was spotted by another boat. When we got on scene just after 0930 over 8 vessels were taking turns letting 2 people enter the water to swim with this shark. We waited patiently for about another hour until we got to see this amazing creature. By the time our group left at 1130 there were over 12 vessels waiting to see the only whale shark for the day. The guides were respectful to each other and enforced that only 2 people can swim at a time and not to touch the animal. We got within a meter from it at one point as it surfaced to forage on plankton. It appeared to be indifferent to the people and boats around it. The tour guide said that peak season is July, which ironically is also hurricane season when it gets more troublesome.
This individual was located during a whale shark spot mapping survey conducted by the Vermilion Sea Institute. Data collected on this shark was submitted to Sharkbook. https://www.sharkbook.ai/
